newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pull back at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pull back at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks erased slim gains at the close on profit-taking Friday and were expected to switch back to gains early next week, dealers said.
"This dip will help consolidate the market's recent advance," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli. "Many people decided it was best today to lock in some profits."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.4 percent to 822.5, trimming gains in the week to 1.1 percent.
The session featured a rollercoaster ride by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which first surged 15 percent but closed up only 1.0 percent after rumors of a buyout were denied.

"Nobody knows quite what to think about Celulosa, but something obviously is in the works, and it probably has to do with some kind of foreign cash injection even if it's just a financing scheme or joint venture," another trader said.
The stock closed up 27 percent on the week at $0.74, against a ceiling of $1.2 in the last 12 months.
The MerVal, in contrast, stands at a five-year high.

Floor volume remained strong Friday but shrank to 35.2 million pesos from Thursday's huge turnover of 52.1 million pesos. Over-the-counter deals dwindled to 82 million pesos from 158 million Thursday.
"It would have been hard today to match that kind of volume, so this late drop doesn't surprise me," one analyst said.
The broad market index dipped 0.2 percent, with winners smashing losers 40 to 28 and 19 stocks closing flat.
Best main-tier performers besides Celulosa were Banco Frances, which tacked on 1.1, and construction stock Polledo and steelmaker Siderca, both up 0.8 percent.
MerVal losers were led by electricity generator Central Costanera, oil company Astra and sugar refiner Ledesma, which declined 2.8 percent, 2.5 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
